artifacts.summary: Rules the mandate should be extended narrowly: synchronous nested subagent delegation is unaffected, but ending a turn to await an async/backgrounded subagent dispatch is prohibited outright (not bounded with a deadline, since no PID/status poll primitive exists for it, unlike the CI and local-gate cases). Finds the cited stranding incident was a misdiagnosis with no confirmed hazard, while the async-dispatch capability itself is real and already used once (the fork-probe incident). Recommends exact wording for general-implementation-agent.md's Local Long-Running Command Discipline, cross-reference pointers in bounded-build-waiter.md/external-process-wait.md, and a new probe-diagnostic subsection in orchestrate-state-machine.md's Abandoned Wrap-Up area. Does not reopen stall_suspected's trigger.

memory_candidates.content: When extending a bounded-wait mandate (CI-poll / local-PID-kill-0 style) to a new case, check whether the new case actually has a foreground-pollable liveness/status primitive before copying the deadline-and-poll shape. A harness-level async Agent-tool dispatch has none (no PID, no status call reachable from inside the dispatching turn -- the Agent tool's own contract is 'don't peek, don't race, the notification arrives later as a message'), so the correct rule for that case is a flat prohibition on backgrounding-and-waiting, not a bounded-deadline allowance. Verify the mechanism exists before transferring a pattern 'almost verbatim'.

When diagnosing whether an externally-watched dispatch is alive or stranded, use artifact mtimes (actively advancing = alive) and live child-process checks, never 'has its closing artifact (e.g. handoff file) appeared yet' -- some phases (e.g. research in this codebase) never write a handoff in any mode, and more generally 'hasn't reached its closing write yet' is indistinguishable from 'never will' using presence/absence alone.
